meta.purpose: Every value that could not be confirmed from an official source, and every inconsistency found between official sources, is recorded here and published on the Flagged for Review page. Flags do not block publication.

severity_scale.high: A headline figure is missing or two official sources disagree on a headline figure.
severity_scale.medium: A supporting figure is missing, or a figure is only valid for a location/condition that may not be yours.
severity_scale.low: Presentational or labelling inconsistency; no number is in doubt.

flags.title: Citi publishes no readable savings APY
flags.field: Citi Savings — APY, minimum deposit, monthly fee

flags.title: Discover Bank is no longer an active FDIC-insured institution
flags.field: Institution status
flags.what_happened: FDIC BankFind records Discover Bank as ACTIVE=0 with an end-effective date of 05/18/2025. Independently, https://www.discover.com/online-banking/savings-account/ redirects to Capital One's 360 Performance Savings page. Discover is therefore excluded as a standalone option.

flags.title: Expanded FDIC coverage through partner-bank networks is a program feature, not a higher FDIC limit
flags.field: FDIC coverage up to $3,000,000
flags.what_happened: SoFi advertises 'additional FDIC-insurance up to $3M through a network of participating banks'. The FDIC's own limit is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category. Coverage above that is achieved by sweeping balances to other insured banks under a program agreement, so it depends on the program working as described and on you not already holding deposits at the receiving banks.
flags.action_taken: SoFi's $3M figure is published with this distinction stated on the row and explained on the FDIC page.
flags.how_to_resolve: Read SoFi's footnotes 6 and 7 and the participating-bank list, and check whether you already bank with any receiving institution.

flags.title: Every savings APY on this site is variable and can change without notice
flags.field: All APYs
flags.what_happened: Each institution states that its savings interest rate and APY are variable and may change at any time, before or after the account is opened. Chase adds that website rates are generally updated each business day and may vary by market; Citizens adds that the variable APY may increase or decrease daily after opening.
flags.action_taken: Every published rate carries the institution's own stated effective date plus this site's UTC capture timestamp. All return projections are explicitly labelled as holding the APY constant, which will not happen in practice.
flags.how_to_resolve: Re-check the live rate on the institution's page immediately before funding an account.

flags.title: Headline rates at three big banks require a relationship or new-money condition
flags.field: Headline APY vs. standard APY
flags.what_happened: U.S. Bank's 3.50% requires an eligible U.S. Bank checking/Safe Debit/credit card AND $25,000 in combined qualifying balances; its standard rate is 0.05%. Wells Fargo's 3.25% is for new savings customers only and requires depositing and maintaining $25,000+ within 30 days; its standard Platinum Savings rate is 0.01%. Chase Premier Savings' 0.02% is a relationship rate requiring a linked checking account and five customer-initiated transactions per statement period; the standard rate is 0.01%.
flags.action_taken: Both the conditional rate and the standard rate are published for each of these products, and a 'Conditions' column marks which rates are conditional.
flags.how_to_resolve: Decide whether you will actually meet and keep meeting the condition. If not, use the standard rate when comparing.
